slides.title: Iterable vs Iterator Protocol
slides.prompt: An iterable is an object with an __iter__() method that returns an iterator. An iterator is an object with a __next__() method that returns elements one at a time and raises StopIteration when empty.

slides.title: Built-in Iterator Creator
slides.prompt: Fill in the built-in function name used to obtain an iterator from an iterable object.

slides.title: End of Iteration Exception
slides.prompt: Which exception is raised by __next__() when an iterator has no more items?

slides.title: Fetching Next Element
slides.prompt: Fill in the built-in function used to advance an iterator and retrieve its next value.

slides.title: Safe Next with Default Value
slides.prompt: How can you prevent a StopIteration exception when manually stepping through an iterator?
options: By passing a default fallback value as the second argument to next(it, default)
By calling iter.has_next() before calling next()
By wrapping the iterator inside a tuple automatically
Iterators never raise errors if wrapped in a list
slides.correctAnswer: By passing a default fallback value as the second argument to next(it, default)

slides.title: Dunder Iter Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method name required to make an object iterable.

slides.title: Iterator Exhaustion
slides.prompt: What happens when you try to loop over a fully consumed (exhausted) iterator a second time?
options: The loop completes immediately without yielding any items
It restarts iteration automatically from the first element
It converts the iterator into a list automatically
slides.correctAnswer: The loop completes immediately without yielding any items
